title: БИОЛОГИЯ И ЭКОЛОГИЯ РАСТЕНИЯ ЛОПУХА БОЛЬШОГО (ARCTIUM LAPPA) В РЕСПУБЛИКЕ КАРАКАЛПАКСТАН И ЕГО ЗНАЧЕНИЕ В НАРОДНОМ ХОЗЯЙСТВЕ
abstract: В статье рассматриваются биологические, морфологические и экологические особенности лопуха большого (Arctium lappa L.), произрастающего в условиях Республики Каракалпакстан. Анализируются особенности его роста и развития, строение корневой системы, размножение, распространение и адаптация к различным экологическим факторам. Особое внимание уделяется влиянию засушливого климата, высоких температур, дефицита водных ресурсов и засоления почв на жизнедеятельность растения. Рассматриваются химический состав, лекарственные и пищевые свойства лопуха, а также перспективы его использования в медицине, пищевой промышленности и сельском хозяйстве. Обосновывается необходимость комплексного изучения природных популяций, разработки научно обоснованных методов культивирования и рационального использования растительных ресурсов региона.

title: Định hướng phát triển các sản phẩm du lịch mới phát huy lợi thế trên địa bàn thành phố Đồng Nai thời kỳ kỷ nguyên số
abstract: Bài báo nghiên cứu đánh giá thực trạng và gợi mở những định hướng sáng tạo sản phẩm du lịch mới cho thành phố Đồng Nai trong thời đại công nghệ số. Dù được thiên nhiên và lịch sử ưu đãi với nguồn tài nguyên sinh thái, văn hóa đa dạng như Vườn Quốc gia Cát Tiên, Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên văn hóa Đồng Nai hay di tích Văn Miếu Trấn Biên, việc đưa giải pháp số vào khai thác hoạt động du lịch tại địa phương còn khá hạn chế, chưa khai phóng hết năng lực tiềm tàng. Thông qua tiếp cận dữ liệu thứ cấp cùng phân tích thực địa định tính ở các điểm tham quan, mô hình lưu trú cộng đồng và sản phẩm địa phương, nghiên cứu đề xuất 4 nhóm giải pháp sản phẩm du lịch tiên phong: (1) Sinh thái thông minh; (2) Tái hiện di sản văn hóa qua công nghệ VR/AR; (3) Số hóa bản đồ ẩm thực cùng làng nghề truyền thống; (4) Hệ thống kết nối mạng lưới homestay và du lịch trong cộng đồng. Bài báo nghiên cứu mang đến các khuyến nghị quan trọng về đào tạo nhân lực và năng lực quản trị số, hỗ trợ thành phố Đồng Nai nâng cao vị thế cạnh tranh và tăng trưởng du lịch một cách bền vững.

title: When purchase intentions weakly translate into willingness to pay: a preliminary framework of culturally distorted markets through the case of Rakija, a traditional Balkan spirit
abstract: Purpose This study examines consumer behavior in traditional food markets, focusing on the relationship between perceived value, purchase intentions and willingness to pay. While existing research generally assumes that higher perceived quality leads to greater willingness to pay, this relationship may not hold in culturally embedded markets characterized by informal production and non-market consumption patterns. The paper introduces culturally distorted markets as a preliminary boundary-condition framework to explain this phenomenon, rather than as a validated theory. Design/methodology/approach Using the case of rakija, a traditional fruit brandy widely produced and consumed in Serbia, the study investigates how cultural factors shape consumer behavior and influence market outcomes. A conceptual model incorporating cultural impact, consumer involvement, attitudes, purchase intentions and willingness to pay is tested using survey data collected from 393 consumers. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) is employed to assess the relationships between the constructs. Findings The results confirm that cultural impact significantly influences consumer involvement and attitudes. Attitudes, in turn, are only marginally related to purchase intentions, while consumer involvement shows a stronger association. However, the relationship between purchase intentions and willingness to pay is weak and non-significant. This observed pattern is compatible with the proposed framework; it should not be interpreted as proof of a null effect or as a demonstrated structural break. Originality/value This study introduces the concept of culturally distorted markets, defined as markets in which cultural norms, informal production and non-market reference points disrupt the expected relationship between perceived value and price. Price may cease to function as a reliable signal of quality in such contexts and conventional premium positioning strategies may face structural limitations. The findings are relevant to producers of traditional food products beyond rakija, but these are identified as potentially comparable contexts for future testing rather than as empirically generalizable markets. However, it should be emphasized that the concept is presented as a proposed framework requiring further validation rather than a fully established theory.

title: When does digital technology adoption matter for internationalization? The role of family ownership and innovation investment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether digital technology adoption is consistently related to firms' likelihood of exporting or whether this relationship depends on firm-specific characteristics, particularly family ownership and innovation investment, within the socioemotional wealth (SEW) framework. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 2,570 Italian manufacturing firms with 5–499 employees surveyed in 2022, we empirically test a model in which digital technology adoption, family ownership, and innovation investment jointly explain variation in firms' likelihood of exporting. The hypotheses are tested using probit regression models with interaction effects and average marginal effects. Findings The results show that digital technology adoption is positively related to firms' likelihood of exporting. However, this relationship is not homogeneous. Family ownership positively moderates the relationship between digital technology adoption and export likelihood, indicating that this relationship is stronger among family firms once digital technologies are adopted. Moreover, the positive moderating role of family ownership is stronger among firms reporting innovation investment. Practical implications Managers should approach digital technology adoption as a strategic process rather than a purely technological investment, aligning digital investments with innovation investment, organizational structures, and export strategy, while supporting product adaptation, customer analytics, and foreign market learning. In particular, family firms can leverage their long-term orientation to enhance the export-related value of digital investments. Policymakers should support firms through integrated digital and innovation policies to foster international competitiveness. Originality/value This paper contributes to the literature by challenging universalistic views of digital technology adoption and adopting a conditional perspective on exporting within the broader internationalization process. It shows that the relationship between digital technology adoption and export likelihood depends on family ownership and innovation investment, offering new insights into how family firms may connect digital investments with international growth.

title: When Medicine Refuses to Admit It Was Wrong
abstract: Medicine has always involved uncertainty, but we do not always admit this as openly as we should. We are trained to make decisions under pressure, often with incomplete information and little time to weigh the consequences. Patients look to us for answers, families want reassurance, and our colleagues expect us to be confident in our actions. Still, history shows that some treatments we once thought essential turned out to be ineffective or even harmful. After over forty years in medicine, much of it spent caring for critically ill patients, I have seen many treatments rise and fall in popularity. I have watched medications hailed as breakthroughs, procedures adopted as standard practice, and recommendations defended passionately, only to be questioned when new evidence appeared. This is not a failure of science; in fact, it is how science is supposed to work. The real problem comes when we are so attached to a belief that we ignore evidence that challenges it.

title: Virtual Library Network (VLN): assessing software integration, security and feasibility among university libraries in Bangladesh
abstract: Purpose The purpose of study is to explore the development of a Virtual Library Network (VLN) in university libraries in Bangladesh, focusing on software integration, security and overall feasibility. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted with 220 information professionals from public and private universities in Bangladesh. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney U tests, Kruskal–Wallis tests and binary logistic regression. Findings The study found that while library software generally met basic functional needs, there were gaps in analytics, integration and vendor support. Security measures were well-perceived, but improvements were needed in areas like firewall and malware protection. Adoption of traditional integration standards like MARC21 and Z39.50 is high, while newer protocols such as Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting (OAI-PMH) show lower uptake. Major barriers to VLN development included financial constraints, lack of collaboration and insufficient training. Gender and age influence user perceptions of software and privacy policies. Practical implications This study bridges VLN theory and practice by providing empirical evidence from Bangladeshi university libraries and cloud-based integration, interoperability standards, and institutional collaboration are critical for VLN feasibility. Findings guide library administrators in selecting interoperable software, adopting standards such as MARC21, Z39.50, SRU/SRW and Preservation Metadata: Implementation Strategies (PREMIS), enhancing security, privacy, and professional readiness. For policymakers, results support strategies and funding for digital library networking. Originality/value This is one of the first studies to explore VLN development in Bangladesh, providing unique insights into the challenges and opportunities for digital transformation in university libraries in developing countries.

title: US-China Relations in the New Balance of Power in Asia: Hope, Despair and Hedging
journal: Malaysian Journal of History, Politics and Strategic Studies
abstract: This article examines the dual dynamics of hope and despair in the evolving relationship between the United States and China, and their implications for Asia’s emerging balance of power. It argues that the relationship is best understood not as a linear movement towards either war or reconciliation, but as a condition of managed rivalry in which selective cooperation coexists with deepening strategic competition. It asks how the intensification of this rivalry is reshaping the strategic options of Asia’s smaller states, and argues that the rivalry raises the cost and complexity of hedging without foreclosing it, thereby connecting two literatures, on US-China rivalry and on Southeast Asian hedging, that have largely developed in isolation. Drawing on realist, liberal and hedging perspectives, and employing a qualitative, historical-analytical approach, the article traces the evolution of Sino-American relations from Cold War hostility through engagement to contemporary strategic rivalry, before analysing the relationship across five dimensions: the historical, economic, military-security, ideological-governance, and regional-institutional. It shows that the return of the Trump administration in 2025 has not altered the structural foundations of the rivalry but has transformed its expression: from the institutionalised “managed competition” of the Biden years to a more transactional pattern of coercive bargaining punctuated by a fragile trade truce. Cooperation persists in narrower forms, even as structural distrust continues to intensify around trade, technology, Taiwan, the South China Sea, alliance politics and the competing regional visions embodied in the Belt and Road Initiative and the Free and Open Indo-Pacific strategy. For Asian states, particularly ASEAN members that have long hedged between the two powers, intensifying rivalry is progressively narrowing the strategic space for ambiguity and active neutrality. The article concludes that Asia’s stability will depend not only on Washington and Beijing’s capacity to manage their competition responsibly, but also on the ability of regional states to preserve strategic autonomy amid the hardening contours of great power rivalry.

title: Two number 27S OF Philosophical transactions (1667): blood transfusion, priority, and editorial authority
journal: Notes and Records: the Royal Society journal of the history of science
abstract: Abstract In July 1667, during Henry Oldenburg's imprisonment in the Tower of London, the issue numbered 27 of Philosophical Transactions printed an English version of Jean-Baptiste Denis's report of the first documented human blood transfusions. After his release, Oldenburg repudiated the issue and published a replacement number 27 that defended English priority and displaced the French report from the journal's numbered sequence and annual index. Comparison of the two issues, Royal Society meeting records, and later historiography shows that the episode was neither a modern retraction nor simple suppression. Philosophical Transactions remained Oldenburg's private enterprise, and the July issue appropriated its serial identity without his authorization. Yet the replacement was partisan: it foregrounded English precedence in animal transfusion while Denis and Paul Emmerez retained priority in the human procedure. The two number 27s show how numbering, pagination, editorial framing, and indexing became instruments for establishing authority and organizing scientific memory.

title: Word of Mouth, Social Media, and Service Quality on Consumer Purchase Decisions at Culinary Businesses in Surakarta, Indonesia
abstract: Purpose— This study examines the associations of word of mouth, social-media engagement, and perceived service quality with reported culinary purchase decisions among consumers in Surakarta, Indonesia. Research Methodology— A quantitative, cross-sectional questionnaire survey involved 150 purposively selected consumers who used social media and had recently visited local culinary establishments. Reported relationships were estimated using PLS-SEM. Results— Social media had the largest reported positive standardized coefficient (β = 0.518), followed by service quality (β = 0.290) and word of mouth (β = 0.180). The model explained 78.2% of variation in the purchase-decision scores. Research limitations/Implications— Purposive recruitment, reliance on self-reports, possible item overlap, and limited reporting of discriminant validity and bootstrapping constrain causal and population-level inference. The findings support context-specific attention to digital information, recommendations, and service encounters. Originality— The study compares three commonly examined predictors within a single model of culinary-consumer evaluations in Surakarta, highlighting their different estimated magnitudes rather than asserting new causal mechanisms.
